numbers.interpretation: ANOMALY, DO NOT REPORT AT FACE VALUE: ctrl-llm's 9.37 hard R@1 is ~60x every model ever measured on this benchmark, incl. 8B specialists. Suspected mechanism: the LLM arm used the MathNet paper's own Appendix F rewriter prompt, i.e., trained on the benchmark's GENERATION RECIPE — the model learns the generator's stylistic fingerprint, not mathematical equivalence (no item-level leakage: LLM-arm sources are anchor-excluded train-side problems). Discriminating test = OOD eval on REAL mined-duplicate equivalence (job 49587994): if ctrl-llm's advantage vanishes there while ctrl-cas holds, the finding becomes 'synthetic retrieval benchmarks are gameable by recipe-matching; verified supervision generalizes' — a stronger paper claim than the original plan.

numbers.description: Both controlled-experiment arms + bases on REAL equivalence (mined cross-language duplicates, strict metric)
numbers.interpretation: (1) CIRCULARITY CONFIRMED: ctrl-llm's colossal benchmark advantage (9.37 vs 0.13 hard R@1; 61.9 vs 17.3 easy) vanishes entirely on real equivalence (64.4 vs 61.3, within noise on 393 queries) — its MathNet-Retrieve gains are recipe-matching, and notably the recipe transfers ACROSS generators (our pairs came from Qwen3-32B, the benchmark's from Gemini-3-flash; the shared element is the prompt template). (2) NEW FINDING: BOTH synthetic-training arms cause catastrophic forgetting on real-duplicate retrieval (base 84.7 -> ~62-64; more CAS data -> worse, 47.6). Real-world equivalence retrieval appears to be mostly about robust general representations, which narrow synthetic fine-tuning erodes. V1/V2 (replay-mixed, still training) is the direct test of whether mixing fixes this.

numbers.prediction_check: PARTIALLY REFUTED: ctrl-llm DOES beat ctrl-cas on MELD (+9.45 R@1, matching Qwen3-4B) and degrades less on BRIGHT. Refined interpretation: the LLM arm's advantage forms a GRADIENT tracking eval-construction style — enormous on same-recipe (MathNet-Retrieve hard, 66x), moderate on same-genre LLM-rewrite pairs (MELD, 2x; MELD pairs are themselves LLM-constructed then human-verified), zero on organic duplicates (our set, p~0.13), negative-to-zero on naturalistic retrieval (BRIGHT, both arms below base). The 66x headline gap still does not transfer anywhere near proportionally; but the paper's claim must be stated as a recipe-proximity gradient, not a binary vanishing. Also: ctrl-cas is the WORST external generalizer (BRIGHT-tt 1.83 vs base 21.24), and mixing (V1/V2) again rescues most of it (15-17).

config_notes: Training max_seq_length inconsistency (documented 2026-07-29): phase-1 (49569452) trained with --max-seq-length 1024; controlled arms + V1/V2 + seed jobs trained UNCAPPED (model default 32768) because train_controlled_exp/train_phase2/train_ctrl_param omit the flag — harmless for CAS/LLM/mixed pairs (short texts; controlled job completed identically to phase-1 patterns) but OOM-fatal for SABER's long docs (job 49589998). saber_attack.slurm now pins 1024. Effective truncation difference is negligible for the short-text arms; noted for exactness.

JSON-escape defect found 2026-07-30 (job 49630276 post-mortem): the shared extract_json() rejects LaTeX control words inside JSON strings (\mathbb, \sigma, \(  -> json.loads raises, whole call discarded) and SILENTLY corrupts the legal-escape subset (\frac -> FORMFEED+'rac'). Fix: extract_json_robust()/repair_json_escapes() added in generate_llm_pairs.py; the original extract_json is FROZEN byte-identical because every published corpus under data/ was parsed by it. AUDIT (done before the fix) — RETRACTED AND RESTATED 2026-07-31 by the round-3 data audit (finding D-L3). It originally read: 'all 28 .jsonl corpora under data/ were scanned for control-character corruption — NONE found, so no published result is tainted.' That is FALSE as written: it scanned raw file text, where control characters are JSON-ESCAPED and therefore invisible. Re-sweeping the DECODED string values of all 43 .jsonl files under data/ finds 29,181 C0 control characters in 5,262 rows across 21 files. Where they are: 28,356 of them (9,452 x 3 tiers, 1,617 rows each) are in the UPSTREAM cached MathNet-Retrieve corpus, which is byte-identical across tiers and shared by every arm, so it is common-mode and cannot generate an arm gap. In this project's own generated training files the rates are trace-level and too small to move any reported effect: D1 5/6,145 rows, D2 3/6,553, D3 14/5,591, D4 1/6,768, phase-2 3/30,323. The one materially exposed file is data/saber_attack/pairs_summary_channel.jsonl at 52/4,733 rows (1.10%) against the doc channel's 10/11,461 -- i.e. the corruption falls on the label arm that WINS, so +0.0354 is a lower bound (finding D-H2). The corrected conclusion: no published number is plausibly changed, but the blanket 'NONE found' assurance did not hold on its own contemporaneous inputs; the observed cost was discarded calls only, at per-call generation JSON failure rates of 3.3/4.9/9.5/17.9% across the four production runs. Also: the MELD smoke gate was rewritten from a raw pair-count threshold (statistically meaningless at n=2 calls) to per-call JSON success rate >=90% over 12 calls plus a >=20-pairs-per-successful-call floor, and the stale-smoke resume trap was closed.

MELD attack 49639491 (2026-07-30): the residual generation failures are SCHEMA DRIFT, not truncation. CORRECTED 2026-07-31: an earlier diagnosis of these as max_tokens truncation was wrong. Re-parsing all 25 released failure dumps with the live parser: 16 of 25 BALANCE EARLY (the JSON structure closes at chars 1,130-7,531 of completions 12,191-19,312 chars long), so those completions were not cut off at all. The real failure is the model dropping the entry_1/entry_2 wrapper and emitting a bare {topic,framing,statement} object plus a stray brace. What misled the original diagnosis: dump_gen_failure() keeps only the first 8,192 chars, so every dump LOOKS cut off, and the completion_chars values cluster high simply because verbose calls are the ones that drift -- a clustering we read as evidence of a token cap. SECOND FINDING: SamplingParams pins seed=args.seed for every call and the continuation prompt is unchanged for a zero-yield domain, so a domain that fails once re-emits the BYTE-IDENTICAL completion every round -- verified, two groups of 5 md5-identical dumps -- which means 26 of the 27 heldout domain pairs actually produced data, matching meld_pairs_summary_heldout.json's 26 rows_by_domain keys. FIXES APPLIED 2026-07-31, once job 49658160 had exited: (1) dump_gen_failure now keeps 6 KB from EACH end with an explicit elision marker, so 'was it cut off?' is answerable from the dump -- the head-only dump is precisely what misled the original diagnosis; (2) each generation call now draws its own SamplingParams seed from (args.seed, call index), passed as a per-prompt LIST so the batch is preserved, which makes a retry an actual retry instead of a byte-identical re-emission. STILL OPEN: salvaging the longest valid prefix of a drifted pairs array, which would recover ~28 of 30 pairs from a failed call rather than discarding all of them. No published number is affected: the 28-corpus audit found no corruption, and unparsed calls are dropped, never partially ingested.
